facts.statement: Pelorosaurus is a genus of titanosauriform sauropod dinosaur meaning "monstrous lizard".
facts.quote: Pelorosaurus ( ; meaning "monstrous lizard") is a genus of titanosauriform sauropod dinosaur.

facts.statement: Thomas Holtz estimated the length of Pelorosaurus at 24 meters.
facts.quote: Thomas Holtz estimated its length at 24 m.

facts.statement: Pelorosaurus lived in England during the Early Cretaceous period, approximately 140 to 125 million years ago.
facts.quote: Remains referred to Pelorosaurus date from the Early Cretaceous period, about 140–125 million years ago, and have been found in England.

facts.statement: Gideon Mantell identified Pelorosaurus as a land-dwelling dinosaur.
facts.quote: Mantell identified Pelorosaurus as a dinosaur, living on land.

facts.statement: Gideon Mantell originally intended to name the genus "Colossosaurus" but changed it after learning that the Greek word meant "statue" rather than "giant".
facts.quote: Mantell had originally, in November 1849, intended to use the name "Colossosaurus", but upon discovering that kolossos was Greek for "statue" and not "giant", he changed his mind.

facts.statement: The generic name Pelorosaurus is derived from the Greek word pelor, meaning "monster".
facts.quote: The generic name is derived from the Greek pelor, "monster".

facts.statement: Gideon Mantell acquired the large humerus used to describe Pelorosaurus for 8 pounds.
facts.quote: Mantell acquired the bone for £8.

facts.statement: The shape of the humerus, designed to support body weight vertically and possessing a medullary cavity, indicated that Pelorosaurus was a land animal.
facts.quote: The humerus, clearly shaped to vertically support the weight of the body and presumed to possess a medullary cavity, showed that Pelorosaurus was a land animal.

facts.statement: Pelorosaurus became a "wastebasket taxon" used to classify various fragmentary European sauropods from the Early Cretaceous.
facts.quote: Pelorosaurus thus came to be a typical wastebasket taxon for any European sauropod of this period.

facts.statement: In 2007, researchers Michael P. Taylor and Darren Naish proposed to petition the ICZN to make Pelorosaurus conybeari the type species and abandon the name Cetiosaurus brevis.
facts.quote: In 2007, Michael P. Taylor and Darren Naish stated their intention to petition the International Commission on Zoological Nomenclature (ICZN) in order to designate the more widely used name P. conybeari the type species of Pelorosaurus and officially abandon the name C. brevis.

facts.statement: The species Pelorosaurus manseli is considered a nomen dubium and is now classified as Ischyrosaurus manseli.
facts.quote: P. manseli Hulke in Lydekker 1888 (nomen dubium) = Ischyrosaurus manseli

facts.statement: The species Pelorosaurus humerocristatus is now classified as Duriatitan humerocristatus.
facts.quote: P. humerocristatus (Hulke 1874) Sauvage 1887 = Duriatitan humerocristatus.

facts.statement: The species Pelorosaurus armatus is now classified as Oplosaurus armatus.
facts.quote: P. armatus (Gervais 1852) Lydekker 1889 = Oplosaurus armatus

facts.statement: The species Pelorosaurus hulkei is now classified as Ornithopsis hulkei.
facts.quote: P. hulkei (Seeley 1870) Lydekker 1889 = Ornithopsis hulkei

facts.statement: The species Pelorosaurus leedsii is considered a nomen dubium and is now classified as Ornithopsis leedsii.
facts.quote: P. leedsii (Hulke 1887) Lydekker 1890 (nomen dubium) = Ornithopsis leedsii

facts.statement: The species Pelorosaurus praecursor is now classified as Neosodon praecursor.
facts.quote: P. praecursor (Sauvage 1876) Sauvage 1895 = Neosodon praecursor

facts.statement: The species Pelorosaurus mackesoni is considered a nomen dubium and is now classified as Dinodocus mackesoni.
facts.quote: P. mackesoni (Owen 1884) Steel 1970 (nomen dubium) = Dinodocus mackesoni

facts.statement: The species Pelorosaurus megalonyx is considered a nomen dubium and is now classified as Gigantosaurus megalonyx.
facts.quote: P. megalonyx (Seeley 1869) Huene 1909 (nomen dubium) = Gigantosaurus megalonyx

facts.statement: By 1970, researchers John Ostrom and Rodney Steel argued that Richard Owen's claim that Cetiosaurus brevis was a nomen nudum was an inadmissible attempt to change the type specimen.
facts.quote: By 1970 however, both John Ostrom and Rodney Steel understood that Owen's claim that C. brevis in 1842 was still a nomen nudum should be rejected as a transparent attempt to change the type specimen, inadmissible by present standards.

facts.statement: Modern standards suggest that Alexander Melville's renaming of the sauropod bones was incorrect because Cetiosaurus brevis was still available and he should have designated the sauropod bones as the lectotype.
facts.quote: By those same standards though, Melville's name change was also incorrect: as the name Cetiosaurus brevis was still "available" he should simply have made the sauropod bones the lectotype, removing the iguanodontid remains from the syntype series.

facts.statement: Pelorosaurus was the first sauropod to be identified as a dinosaur, even though it was not the first to be discovered.
facts.quote: Pelorosaurus fue el primer saurópodo en ser identificado como dinosaurio, aunque no fue el primero en ser descubierto.

facts.statement: Gideon Mantell originally intended to name the genus "Colossosaurus" in November 1849 but changed his mind after realizing the Greek root meant "statue" rather than "giant".
facts.quote: Mantell tenía originalmente, en noviembre de 1849, la intención de utilizar el nombre de "Colossosaurus", pero al descubrir que ?Kolossos? era griega para "estatua" y no "gigante", cambió de idea.

facts.statement: Gideon Mantell used both the sauropod material of Cetiosaurus brevis and a large humerus found by miller Peter Fuller at the same site, which he assumed belonged to the same individual and was discovered only a few meters from the vertebrae.
facts.quote: Mantell no solo usó el material de saurópodo de C. brevis como el tipo de Pelorosaurus conybeari, sino también un gran húmero encontrado por el molinero Peter Fuller en el mismo sitio, BMNH 28626, que supuso que era del mismo individuo, siendo descubierto solo un a pocos metros de las vértebras.

facts.statement: Gideon Mantell purchased the humerus for 8 pounds.
facts.quote: Mantell adquirió el hueso por 8 £.

facts.statement: Richard Owen resolved the taxonomic issue by designating the humerus as the sole holotype for Pelorosaurus conybeari.
facts.quote: Owen lo resolvió presentando simplemente el húmero como el único holotipo de Pelorosaurus conybeari.

facts.statement: In 1970, John Ostrom and Rodney Steel argued that Owen's claim that Cetiosaurus brevis was a nomen nudum in 1842 should be rejected as a transparent attempt to change the type specimen, which is inadmissible by current standards.
facts.quote: Sin embargo, en 1970, tanto John Ostrom como Rodney Steel entendieron que la afirmación de Owen de que C. brevis en 1842 todavía era un nomen nudum debería rechazarse como un intento transparente de cambiar el espécimen tipo, inadmisible según los estándares actuales.

facts.statement: In life, Pelorosaurus was a medium-sized sauropod compared to the giants of its group, reaching 16 meters in length, 4 meters in height, and weighing 17 tons.
facts.quote: En vida fue un saurópodo de tamaño mediano en comparación con los más gigantes de su grupo, igualmente llegó a medir 16 metros de largo, 4 de alto y a pesar 17 toneladas.

facts.statement: The humerus, clearly formed to support the body weight vertically and presumed to possess a medullary cavity, showed that Pelorosaurus was a terrestrial animal.
facts.quote: El húmero, claramente formado para soportar verticalmente el peso del cuerpo y que se presume posee una cavidad medula , mostró que Pelorosaurus era un animal terrestre.

facts.statement: In 1882, Henri-Émile Sauvage first stated that Pelorosaurus belonged to the Sauropoda.
facts.quote: In 1882 Henri-Émile Sauvage first stated it belonged to the Sauropoda.

facts.statement: In recent years, the material of Pelorosaurus has commonly been placed in the broader group Titanosauriformes.
facts.quote: In recent years, the material was commonly placed in a more general Titanosauriformes.

facts.statement: Pelorosaurus conybeari is the only known species of the extinct genus Pelorosaurus, a braiosaurid sauropod dinosaur that lived at the beginning of the Cretaceous Period, about 132 million years ago during the Barremian, in what is now Europe.
facts.quote: Pelorosaurus conybeari es la única especie conocida del género extinto Pelorosaurus (gr. «lagarto monstruoso») de dinosaurio sauropodo braquiosáurido que vivió a principios del período Cretácico, hace unos 132 millones años durante el Barremiense, en lo que es hoy Europa.

facts.statement: However, according to the same standards, Melville's name change was also incorrect because the name Cetiosaurus brevis was still "available"; he should have simply designated the sauropod bones as the lectotype, removing the iguanodontian remains from the series of syntypes.
facts.quote: Sin embargo, según esos mismos estándares, el cambio de nombre de Melville también fue incorrecto, como el nombre Cetiosaurus brevis todavía estaba "disponible", simplemente debería haber hecho de los huesos del saurópodo el lectotipo , eliminando los restos de iguanodóntidos de la serie de sintipos.

facts.statement: In 2003, paleontologists Upchurch and Martin planned to petition the ICZN to preserve the name Pelorosaurus conybeari and suppress C. brevis.
facts.quote: los paleontólogos Upchurch y Martin hicieron planes para solicitar a la ICZN en 2003 que el tipo Cetiosaurus fuera cambiado de C. brevis a C. oxoniensis, que el nombre Pelorosaurus conybeari fuese preservado, y que C. brevis fuera el único suprimido.

facts.statement: Pelorosaurus was historically a wastebasket taxon containing many poorly defined sauropods.
facts.quote: Pelorosaurus, es un género cajón de sastre donde se ha colocado a una gran cantidad de saurópodos mal definidos

facts.statement: Pelorosaurus belongs to the family Brachiosauridae and may have only three known species: P. conybeari, P. humerocristatus, and P. mackesoni.
facts.quote: Pertenece a la familia Brachiosauridae, y posiblemente solo posea tres especies conocidas, Pelorosaurus conybearei, P. humerocristatus y P. mackesoni.

facts.statement: Mantell was the first to suggest a relationship between Pelorosaurus and dinosaurs.
facts.quote: Mantell fue el primero en sugerir que había una relación entre Pelorosaurus y los dinosaurios.

facts.statement: Friedrich August Quenstedt formally classified Pelorosaurus within Dinosauria in 1852.
facts.quote: En 1852 Friedrich August Quenstedt lo clasificó formalmente dentro de Dinosauria.

facts.statement: Henri-Émile Sauvage declared that Pelorosaurus belonged to the group Sauropoda in 1882.
facts.quote: En 1882 Henri-Émile Sauvage declaró que Pelorosaurus pertenecía al grupo Sauropoda.

facts.statement: In 1927, von Huene placed Pelorosaurus in Brachiosauridae based on a possible relationship with Brachiosaurus.
facts.quote: hasta en 1927 von Huene entiende la posible relación con Brachiosaurus, colocando a Pelorosaurus en Brachiosauridae

facts.statement: In recent years, Pelorosaurus material is commonly placed at the general level of the clade Titanosauriformes.
facts.quote: En los últimos años, el material se coloca comúnmente en un nivel general del clado Titanosauriformes.

facts.statement: The validity of Pelorosaurus is problematic because P. conybeari was based on a humerus and vertebrae discovered separately.
facts.quote: La validez de Pelorosaurus es problemática. P. conybeari se basó en un húmero y vértebras descubiertos por separado.

facts.statement: Pelorosaurus humerocristatus is now considered a synonym of Duriatitan humerocristatus.
facts.quote: P. humerocristatus (Hulke 1874) Sauvage 1887 = Duriatitan humerocristatus.

facts.statement: Pelorosaurus mackesoni is a nomen dubium now assigned to the genus Dinodocus.
facts.quote: P. mackesoni (Owen 1884) Steel 1970 (nomen dubium) = Dinodocus mackesoni

facts.statement: Pelorosaurus lived from the Tithonian to the Albian stages, between 145.06 and 110.1 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Tithonian to Albian (145.06 to 110.1 million years ago)

facts.statement: The humerus measures 137 centimeters in length, suggesting relatively long forelimbs typical of brachiosaurids.
facts.quote: El húmero, mide 137 centímetros de largo lo cual es muy alargado, y esto sugiere un rasgo típico de braquiosáurido: unas extremidades delanteras relativamente largas.

facts.statement: The type species P. conybeari was based on a humerus and vertebrae that were discovered separately.
facts.quote: P. conybeari se basó en un húmero y vértebras descubiertos por separado.

facts.statement: The species P. becklesii was known from a humerus, radius, ulna, and skin impressions.
facts.quote: Una especie notable, P. becklesii, se conocía por el húmero, el radio y el cúbito, así como por las impresiones de la piel.

facts.statement: Pelorosaurus manseli is a nomen dubium now assigned to the genus Ischyrosaurus.
facts.quote: P. manseli Hulke y Lydekker 1888 (nomen dubium) = Ischyrosaurus manseli

facts.statement: Pelorosaurus armatus is now considered a synonym of Oplosaurus armatus.
facts.quote: P. armatus (Gervais 1852) Lydekker 1889 = Oplosaurus armatus

facts.statement: Pelorosaurus hulkei is now considered a synonym of Ornithopsis hulkei.
facts.quote: P. hulkei (Seeley 1870) Lydekker 1889 = Ornithopsis hulkei

facts.statement: Pelorosaurus leedsii is a nomen dubium now assigned to the genus Ornithopsis.
facts.quote: P. leedsii (Hulke 1887) Lydekker 1890 (nomen dubium) = Ornithopsis leedsii

facts.statement: Pelorosaurus praecursor is now considered a synonym of Neosodon praecursor.
facts.quote: P. praecursor (Sauvage 1876) Sauvage 1895 = Neosodon praecursor

facts.statement: Pelorosaurus megalonyx is a nomen dubium now assigned to the genus Gigantosaurus.
facts.quote: P. megalonyx (Seeley 1869) Huene 1909 (nomen dubium) = Gigantosaurus megalonyx
